title: HRes_ETa_SAFER_Aconcagua: a Google Earth Engine workflow for high-resolution SAFER evapotranspiration mapping
description:
Automated, cloud-based framework implemented in Google Earth Engine to estimate actual evapotranspiration (ETa) at 30 m spatial resolution over the Aconcagua River Basin, Chile.

The workflow applies the SAFER (Simple Algorithm for Evapotranspiration Retrieving) algorithm with fixed, historically calibrated coefficients (a = 0.3684, b = -0.0012, derived from a 10-year analysis, 2014-2024) to Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface reflectance and surface temperature, combined with daily reference evapotranspiration (ET0, FAO-56 Penman-Monteith) computed from ERA5-Land reanalysis. A monthly-median gap-filling strategy preserves temporal continuity in cloud-affected periods. Outputs are daily, monthly and annual ETa rasters (mm) at 30 m. The resulting maps are used to assess structural water stress in a semi-arid agricultural basin by contrasting high-resolution water demand against available supply.

This repository contains the source code supporting the article "Assessment of structural water stress in semi-arid agricultural basins using high-resolution evapotranspiration mapping", accepted for publication in Ecohydrology & Hydrobiology (2026).
